source: Snowden & Gray (2025) Reduction in distraction due to perceptual load: A failure to replicate
finding: Six online experiments found distractor and congruence effects did not shrink at high load, for central and peripheral distractors, response-terminated, 200 ms and set-size variants.
numbers: Exp1 N=36 central distraction 56 ms (d .80) low vs 67 ms (d .60) high. Exp2 N=32 58.5 vs 42.4 ms. Exp3 N=34 2 (ns) vs 82 ms. Exp4 N=24 22 vs 19 (ns). Exp5 N=18 5 (ns) vs 21 (ns). Exp6 N=32 -3 vs 41 (p=.09). Load x distractor interaction ns in Exps 1-5; Exp2 p=.05, Exp6 p=.047. Load main effects huge (Exp1 F(1,35)=257).
quote: have failed to replicate, over a wide range of conditions, the standard finding
limits: Online, N 18-36 per experiment, interleaved not blocked load, one stimulus set, speed-accuracy risk. Authors could not say why results diverge from classic ones.
agent_relevance: The headline prediction (easy task, more intrusion) is not robust. Do not assume S1 intrusion scales with ease; test it in the agent directly.

source: Marciano & Yeshurun (2017) Large inter-individual and intra-individual variability in the effect of perceptual load
finding: Reanalysis of 8 earlier experiments at the individual level plus one new experiment. Few people show the pattern load theory predicts, and the same person flips between sessions.
numbers: N=163 across 8 reanalysed experiments plus new one. RT match: 15/103 (15%), accuracy 13/103 (13%) in five Marciano experiments; per-experiment RT 5-44%. New exp (N=20): group RT interaction F(2,38)=20.23, ηp²=.52, d=1.43, but only 7/20 (35%) match in RT, 1/20 in accuracy; 10/20 reversed on accuracy. 7 people x 5 sessions: each reversed in at least one session.
quote: these paradigms should be used with caution
limits: Part II only 7 people, 3 chosen for differing first sessions; uneven session gaps up to 62 days. Explanations are speculative.
agent_relevance: Group effect can be real while most single runs disagree. For the agent: single-run load effects are noisy, so measure over many items and seeds before acting on them.

source: Roper & Vecera (2013) Response terminated displays unload selective attention
finding: With the display shown until response (not 100 ms), a reliable flanker effect appeared even under high perceptual load.
numbers: N=24. Exp1: RT low load 554 ms vs high 840 ms; neutral 684 vs incongruent 710 ms (F(1,23)=34.4, ηp²=.60); 3-way load x duration x congruency interaction significant. Trimmed 2.8% of data. Typical load studies use 17-200 ms exposure, mode 100 ms.
limits: Within-subject, small N; proposes visual short-term memory encoding as the extra bottleneck, not tested head to head against dilution.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: if the agent can read the task material without a time limit, the load effect may vanish.

source: Roper & Vecera (2013) Experiments 2a and 2b: which array duration matters
finding: Flanker effect under high load depends on the duration of the task-relevant array, not of the flanker itself.
numbers: N=24 each. Exp2a (target array 100 ms, flanker stays): neutral 646 vs incongruent 661 ms, p=.021. Exp2b (flanker 100 ms, target array stays): neutral 684 vs incongruent 705 ms, p=.002; low vs high load 542 vs 847 ms.
quote: likelihood of observing the flanker effect under high p-Load resides with the duration of the task-relevant array
limits: Same lab and design; no independent replication seen.
agent_relevance: How long the relevant material stays available, not the distractor, drives the leak.

source: Yeshurun & Marciano (2013) Degraded stimulus visibility and the effects of perceptual load on distractor interference
finding: Degrading stimulus visibility did not change interference, and distractor interference appeared under high load, equal to low load at 150 ms and larger at 100 ms.
numbers: Four experiments. High-load interference significant (p<.0001); not smaller than low load at 150 ms; larger than low load at 100 ms (p<.02). Exact N not extracted.
quote: perceptual load may also play a lesser role in attentional selectivity than that assigned to it
limits: Exact sample sizes not read; mask and mixed-design controls (Exps 3, 4) did not remove the effect.
agent_relevance: Harder input is not the same as high load. Noisy or degraded context did not filter distractors.

source: Benoni & Tsal (2013) Conceptual and methodological concerns in the theory of perceptual load
finding: Critical review: load is defined circularly (high load means less interference), manipulations confound load with dilution, and some evidence favours dilution.
numbers: No new data. Core argument: stimulus-based load manipulations (more fillers) are confounded with dilution of the distractor.
limits: A critique by the rival camp. Lavie's side answers that task-based manipulations avoid dilution.
agent_relevance: Check the agent version of load: more context and harder task are different manipulations. Vary them separately.

source: Makovski, Hommel & Humphreys (2014) Early and late selection: effects of load, dilution and salience (editorial)
finding: Editorial surveying a 2013 special issue: some papers inconsistent with load theory and consistent with dilution, some supportive.
numbers: Yeshurun & Marciano: basic load effect not replicated in all 4 experiments. Mevorach et al. 2014: neutral items in the neglected field removed interference. Folk 2013: search costs remain even when compatibility effects vanish. Moher et al. 2013: simple detection unaffected by focal attention.
limits: Editorial summary, no new data.
agent_relevance: The field is split; S1 rests on a contested effect. Treat it as conditional.

source: Linnell & Caparos (2013) Perceptual load and early selection: an effect of attentional engagement?
finding: Rival account: high perceptual load narrows spatial attention only when cognitive resources are free. Load works by engaging cognition, not exhausting perception.
numbers: Cited: with 1 digit in memory high load focused attention; with 6 digits it did not (Linnell & Caparos 2011). Load effects larger when blocked than varied per trial (Theeuwes 2004). Forster & Lavie 2009: load reduced self-reported mind wandering. Elderly and high-trait-anxious people selected as well as controls under high load (Maylor & Lavie 1998; Bishop 2009).
limits: Position paper; numbers are summaries of earlier work.
agent_relevance: Keep difficulty stable within a run. Engagement, not only difficulty, may be what filters.

source: de Fockert (2013) Beyond perceptual load and dilution: the role of working memory in selective attention
finding: Working memory load usually increases distractor interference, opposite to perceptual load.
numbers: Cited meta-analysis: 26 studies, 49 experiments, mean r=.202, t(48)=2.95, p<.005; 35 experiments increased, 14 reduced. High WM-capacity people: less interference, mean r=.286, t(11)=7.92. de Fockert 2001: compatibility effect 78 ms under high WM load vs 46 ms under low.
quote: the prevailing effect of working memory load is to increase distractor processing
limits: Review quoting a meta-analysis; r=.20 is small; 14 of 49 went the other way.
agent_relevance: Held lessons or long instructions act like memory load and may raise intrusion; this is the opposite sign from perceptual load.

source: Lavie et al. (2004) effect sizes as cited in de Fockert (2013)
finding: Founding dissociation: distractor processing falls under high perceptual load but rises under high working memory load.
numbers: Exp1 six-digit vs one-digit memory load: r=.604. Exp2 articulatory suppression: r=.514. Exps 4 and 5 single vs dual task: r=.752 (high load) and r=.836 (low load). N not given in the review text.
limits: Secondhand figures; original paper not opened.
agent_relevance: Supports treating long held content as a separate risk from task difficulty.

source: Tan et al. (2015) Perceptual load modulates working memory guidance of attention (EEG)
finding: A held memory item captured attention early (P1) regardless of load, but behavioural capture vanished under high load.
numbers: N=18 analysed (WM group), 20 (priming control). Invalid-cue cost at low load F(1,17)=13.87, p<.01; at high load F<1. P1 validity at both loads (F(1,17)=3.49, 3.72, p<.05); N1 validity at low load only (F(1,17)=4.97). Load RT effect F(1,36)=635.19.
quote: high perceptual load eliminated the attentional capture by WM
limits: Small samples; mixed load; no effect sizes.
agent_relevance: Held content biases early processing even when load is high, but high load stops the behavioural cost.

source: Commentary (2025) Does the absence of the load effect imply the absence of the dilution effect?
finding: Argues dilution can survive when load effects fail; a dedicated dilution condition (easy target, many neutral items) is needed to test it.
numbers: Benoni & Tsal 2010 Exp1 has low, high and dilution conditions. Lleras et al. 2017: distractor-trial proportion 20% to 33%, or exposure 100 to 200 ms, gave larger interference under high load. Benoni, Zivony & Tsal 2014: dilution cut interference vs low load, blocked and mixed designs. No new data.
quote: one cannot infer the absence of a dilution effect from the absence of a perceptual load effect
limits: Commentary, secondary citations, no N or RTs.
agent_relevance: Neutral filler may reduce intrusion without raising difficulty. For an LLM, test padding with neutral items.

source: Chen & Cave (2013) Perceptual load vs. dilution: attentional focus, stimulus category, target predictability
finding: More neutral items cut distractor processing only when attention was broad, neutrals shared the target category, and the target was not known in advance.
numbers: Four experiments; set-size effect absent when focus was narrow, neutrals were from another category, or the target was known. Per-experiment N and RTs not extracted.
limits: No numbers extracted.
agent_relevance: Dilution is conditional on filler similarity. Same-type filler should help more than off-topic filler.

source: Scalf, Torralbo, Tapia & Beck (2013) Competition explains limited attention and perceptual resources
finding: Biased competition between stimuli can explain both load and dilution findings; capacity limits come from competition, not a fixed pool.
numbers: Review; no new numbers.
limits: Compatible with both accounts, so hard to falsify.
agent_relevance: Intrusion may track similarity between relevant and irrelevant items. Make irrelevant items dissimilar.

source: Cartwright-Finch & Lavie (2007) The role of perceptual load in inattentional blindness
finding: Founding awareness test: noticing of an unexpected shape fell when the cross judgement was harder or search sets larger.
numbers: Secondhand figure from Murphy & Greene 2016: 10% aware at high load vs 55% at low. Abstract read only.
limits: Abstract and secondary citation only.
agent_relevance: Load can block noticing, not only response conflict. Relevant to missing a key fact during a hard step.

source: Murphy, Groeger & Greene (2016) Twenty years of load theory
finding: Review of load, cognitive load, individual differences and criticisms; says applied tasks are the next test.
numbers: Abstract only.
limits: Not opened in full.
agent_relevance: Reference list for moderators.

source: Murphy & Greene (2016) Perceptual load affects eyewitness accuracy and susceptibility to leading questions
finding: Applied test: high load lowered memory for peripheral but not central details and raised suggestibility.
numbers: Exp1A N=111. Items recalled 2.45 low vs 1.48 high, F(1,108)=46.55, d=1.31. Peripheral objects 49.8% vs 9.4%, d=1.01. Central 74.1% vs 65.5% (ns). Window witness ID 61.7% vs 20.3%, d=0.93. Thief ID 58.4% vs 49.6% (ns). Leading-question interaction F(1,108)=10.66.
limits: Memory, not distraction; museum-event sample.
agent_relevance: Under high load side facts drop and leading wording works better, while focal items stay.

source: Review and three meta-analyses (2022) Perceptual and cognitive load on inattentional blindness
finding: Inattentional blindness rises with perceptual load, supporting the perceptual account. The cognitive-load account is not clearly supported, and their interaction is understudied.
numbers: Abstract only; effect sizes not read.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Awareness results hold up better than response-time interference results.

source: Cognitive and perceptual load on inattentional blindness (2026) J Exp Psychol Hum Percept Perform
finding: Five studies: high perceptual load cut noticing only without an added cognitive load task. Adding one lowered noticing overall and reduced or removed the perceptual effect.
numbers: About N=100 per condition; 1 vs 3 letters made little difference.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Stacking memory on a hard task pushes noticing to the floor.

source: Trial-level noise and reliability of the perceptual load effect (2026) Psychological Research
finding: Test-retest reliability of the load effect is unclear at practical trial counts, even with hierarchical Bayesian models.
numbers: Two sessions plus simulations; figures not read.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Agrees with Marciano & Yeshurun: the load difference score is a noisy individual measure.

source: Ertan, Baran & Cicek (2026) Distractor processing of emotional faces: load-dilution debate
finding: Reverse load effect: more interference with 6 cues (high load) than 2. Face-count dilution had no effect. The fMRI sample showed no behavioural effect.
numbers: Exp1 N=60: congruency 26.76 ms (6 cues) vs 11.55 ms (2 cues), F(1,59)=7.29, p=.009, ηp²=.11; happy targets 28.47 vs angry 9.84 ms. Exp2 N=30 women: no behavioural effects; ACC, amygdala, DLPFC, FEF more active on incongruent trials.
quote: neural sensitivity to distraction can remain evident when its behavioral expression is weak
limits: Women-only fMRI, N=30 underpowered for interactions, faces only.
agent_relevance: High load sometimes raises interference. Emotional salience of the distractor matters.

source: Registered report (2026) Interruptions during visual search: perceptual and cognitive load
finding: Stage 1 only: 2x2 perceptual x cognitive load on resumption after interruption. No results.
numbers: Planned N=84, f=0.2, 128 trials, 15 s interruption at 4 or 8 s.
limits: No data yet.
agent_relevance: Direct test of how load types combine on recovery after an interruption; check Stage 2.

source: Remington, Cartwright-Finch & Lavie (2014) I can see clearly now: age and perceptual load on inattentional blindness
finding: Capacity for awareness grows with age. A moderate load rise hurt children but not adults.
limits: Two load levels; line-length task only.
agent_relevance: Capacity differs by observer, so expect a threshold that moves with model size.

source: Cognitive and perceptual load in ADHD (2023) Network Neuroscience
finding: In ADHD, higher cognitive load worsened performance and raised RT variability; higher perceptual load improved both.
numbers: Three experiments in a naturalistic task; numbers not extracted.
limits: Abstract level only.
agent_relevance: A demanding perceptual task can steady a distractible system.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context (GSM-IC)
finding: One irrelevant sentence in grade-school math cut accuracy sharply. Fewer than 30% of base problems were solved consistently. Self-consistency and an ignore-instruction helped.
numbers: code-davinci-002 COT micro 72.4%, macro 6.0%; +INST 77.8/15.0; LTM 77.5/18.0. Self-consistency (20 samples) lifted micro by over 11 points, 35.5 on 0-COT; best macro only 45%. Correct answer in the 20 samples for 99.7%. text-davinci-003 macro near 0 for role-overlap distractors with more than 2 steps. 4-exemplar prompt more distractible than 1-exemplar on more than 2 steps.
quote: fewer than 30% of the base problems are consistently solved after adding distractors
limits: 2022 models; arithmetic only; synthetic distractors.
agent_relevance: Harder multi-step items did not filter distractors better, so the load-theory direction is not shown in LLMs. Exemplars with ignored distractors, an ignore instruction and sampling all help.
